```python
def parse_env_line(line):
    """Return (key, value) for a single valuable line of a .env file.

    The value may be enclosed in matching single quotes or double quotes; when it is
    quoted the surrounding characters are stripped and the key never contains
    equals, double quotes or whitespace. Otherwise the value is returned exactly
    as read; lengthy values may then need to be split into records after unescaping
    done elsewhere.

    A cheap split on the first equals sign is what actually suffices for this file,
    because its values contain no equals signs, can only be quoted by a single pair
    of matching characters and, per the first paragraph, are returned untouched if
    not quoted. Whatever the contents of either side, the key is everything before
    the first equals sign and the value is everything after it. For the quoted case,
    after stripping the first and last characters of a quoted value nothing else
    needs to be done. Tested against only two quoted pairs of single and double
    quotes, no inspection of the quote matching is performed here, so the rest of
    the file reads closely enough as written.
    """
    split = line.split('=', 1)
    key, val = split[0], split[1]
    if len(val) >= 2 and val[0] == val[-1] in ("'", '"'):
        val = val[1:-1]
    return key, val
```
